title: Connexions projectives et uniformisation : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the previous pages. X/S is smooth of relative dimension r. P = P(E) is a projective bundle over X with a marked section, and the tangent data of the section are identified with Ω ≅ Ω^1_{X/S}. Ŝ is the formal completion of P along the marked section. If the extension defining E is split, Ŝ ≅ Sym^∧(Ω).

What the ∞-projective connection is. An '∞-connexion projective' is an isomorphism φ_∞ : P^∞_{X/S} → Ŝ inducing the given identification on first-order parts. Here P^∞_{X/S} is the pro-object of principal parts, i.e. the formal neighbourhood of the diagonal. Concretely, φ_∞ identifies the formal neighbourhood of each point x in X with the formal neighbourhood of the marked point in the fibre P_x ≅ P^r. It is a formal, relative, algebraic version of a projective (Cartan-type) structure, or 'developing map to order ∞'.

What flatness means. P^∞ carries its canonical stratification Δ : P^∞ → P^∞ ⊗̂ P^∞, given by the coproduct δf ↦ δf + overline{δf}. Transporting Δ through φ_∞ gives a stratification Δ' on Ŝ. The connection is called flat if Δ' comes from a stratification of the whole bundle P, i.e. a flat PGL-connection on P preserving the marked section's formal germ. That stratification is then unique, which justifies 'canonique'.

This page writes the data in local coordinates f_1..f_r.
- P^∞ ≅ O_X[[δf_1..δf_r]] and Ŝ ≅ O_X[[T_1..T_r]].
- φ_∞ is given by the images F_i of the T_i, with F_i = δf_i + G_i and G_i of order ≥ 2. The order-≥2 condition says φ_∞ is tangent to the identity, since Ω ≅ Ω^1.
- The inverse is given by Φ_i = T_i + Ψ_i, with Ψ_i of order ≥ 2.

The transported structure Δ' : Ŝ → P^∞ ⊗̂ Ŝ ≅ P^∞[[T_1..T_r]] is determined by the images of the T_i. These are obtained in three steps:
1. Apply Δ to F_i = δf_i + G_i. This gives F_i evaluated at δf + overline{δf}; coefficients in the left O_X stay, those in the right are Taylor-expanded.
2. Push forward along id ⊗ φ_∞ : P^∞ ⊗̂ P^∞ → P^∞ ⊗̂ Ŝ.
3. In effect, substitute overline{δf_j} ↦ Φ_j(T), with appropriately translated coefficients.

Schematically, Δ'(T_i) = F_i(x ; δf + Φ(T)) in P^∞[[T]]. The page ends at 'Posant', just before introducing notation. The evident next step is to write the flatness condition: for each i, the series Δ'(T_i) in T, with coefficients in P^∞, must be a projective-linear (linear-fractional) transformation of the T's. For r = 1 this should reduce to a Schwarzian-type condition.

The next page switches to the Hodge filtration and the symplectic pairing on H^1_dR of a relative curve. This suggests the goal is uniformisation of families of curves via projective structures (indigenous bundles, Kodaira–Spencer / Gauss–Manin).
errors: The transcription (and possibly the manuscript, as a slip) writes O_S[[δf_1..δf_r]] and O_S[[T_1..T_r]], and the previous page has Ω ≅ O_S^r. Since P^∞_{X/S} and Ŝ are sheaves of O_X-algebras, these should be O_X[[δf]], O_X[[T]] and Ω ≅ O_X^r (locally on X).

There is a minor gap, not an error. When computing Δ(F_i), the O_X-coefficients of G_i in the second tensor factor must be Taylor-expanded via the right O_X-structure. The note says this implicitly ('avec ses 2 structures' on the previous page) but does not write it out.
The page is unfinished: it stops at 'Posant' before the explicit flatness condition is stated.

ideas.what: Define an ∞-projective connection as an isomorphism between the formal neighbourhood of the diagonal P^∞_{X/S} and the formal completion Ŝ of a projective bundle along a marked section, tangent to the identity.
ideas.modern_name: Formal/algebraic projective structure (Cartan connection of projective type; jet-theoretic projective structure; in dimension 1, indigenous bundle / oper data)
ideas.usually_credited_to: E. Cartan (projective connections). Gunning (projective structures on Riemann surfaces, 1960s). Algebraic and p-adic versions: Mochizuki (indigenous bundles, 1990s), Beilinson–Drinfeld (opers).
ideas.where_published: The stratification formalism is in Grothendieck, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968) and EGA IV §16. I am not aware of this specific definition appearing in his published texts.

ideas.what: Flatness of the projective connection: the transported stratification on Ŝ extends to a stratification of the whole projective bundle P, and that extension is then unique.
ideas.modern_name: Flatness / integrability of a Cartan connection; flat PGL_{r+1}-connection with compatible section (developing map)

ideas.what: Coordinate computation: φ_∞ given by F_i = δf_i + G_i, its inverse by Φ_i = T_i + Ψ_i, and the transported coaction Δ'(T_i) obtained by substituting into the coproduct δf ↦ δf + overline{δf}.
ideas.modern_name: Formal-groupoid coaction / Hopf-algebroid comodule structure, written in coordinates

missed.claim: Grothendieck set up a characteristic-free, relative, arbitrary-dimension definition of projective structures as formal isomorphisms P^∞_{X/S} ≅ Ŝ, with flatness defined via stratifications. The page breaks off before the explicit flatness equations (presumably a higher-dimensional Schwarzian-type condition). This is a crystalline-style treatment of projective structures aimed at uniformisation, anticipating aspects of Mochizuki's indigenous-bundle formalism. However, the mathematical content is largely known in modern form.
missed.quote: On a donc la structure sur O_S[[T_1,...,T_r]] = Ŝ →(Δ') P^∞_{X/S} ⊗̂ Ŝ ... déduite par transport de structure de celle de P^∞_{X/S}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of historical interest: Grothendieck was treating projective connections and uniformisation through stratifications and principal parts, in arbitrary characteristic. The previous page also raises the open question of whether Σ is canonically determined without dimension or characteristic hypotheses. Little of this appears to be new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an unfinished, routine coordinate computation inside a formalism that is conceptually interesting: projective structures via principal parts and stratifications, linked to uniformisation. The ideas correspond to known notions (Cartan/Gunning projective structures, indigenous bundles, opers). Its historical interest lies in Grothendieck's framing, not in a new result.
transcription_corrections: 'Γ_S O_S[[δf_1,...,δf_r]]' is likely Γ(X, O_X[[δf_1..δf_r]]) or an abbreviation; the 'S' under Γ may be a subscript for the sheaf. The struck-through word before O_S in the Φ_i line is illegible ('Sym^∧'?).
'G_i d'ordre ≥ 2' is in the manuscript as 'G_i d'ordre ≥ 2' (correct).
In the Δ' line the left-hand side appears to read 'O_S[[T_1,...,T_r]] = Ŝ', with a struck-out symbol; the arrow is labelled Δ'.
In the image line, the manuscript has 'Δ(δf_i + G_i) ∈ Γ P^∞ ⊗̂ P^∞', with a crossed-out symbol before δf_i.
